A 3x3 conv on edge 5 already feeds node 3 with conv features, so the direct conv's marginal gain shrinks.
Without the direct 0->3 edge, the output depends on edges 4 and 5, so a conv on edge 5 matters more.
Without the direct edge, all signal passes through node 1 or 2, so a stronger first hop matters more.
When edge 1 is removed, edge 2 is the only feed into node 2, so its conv determines what edge 5 receives.
Two parallel 3x3 first hops from the input are largely substitutes for feature extraction.
Chaining pool after pool on 0->2->3 over-smooths features, especially at the low resolution of ImageNet16.
A conv-rich route already provides spatial capacity, so a cheap direct 1x1 adds little.
With the direct 0->3 edge removed, a shallow identity route into node 2 gives a useful gradient shortcut.
Without the direct edge, the 0->1->2->3 route is a main source of depth, so its middle conv matters more.
